clue.text: A morsel of exotic rum baba

indicators.note: 'of' here means 'taken out of', so the letters sit inside the run of words exotic rum baba

explanation.surface: A tiny bite of a rum-soaked baba from some exotic patisserie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is the hidden-word signal: the answer runs across exotiC RUM Baba.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a small fragment of bread or cake, so it is a morsel.

clue.text: Younger son's joint — a place at Sandhurst

parts.note: a cadet is a younger son, so younger son's gives cadet's
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A younger son's share of the family estate, or a place at the military academy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is the British Army's officer training academy, whose trainees are officer cadets.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadetship is the position of being an officer cadet, a place on a military training course.

clue.text: Remove garrison from a French island

parts.note: un is French for a
the Isle of Man is an island

explanation.surface: Withdraw troops from an island belonging to France.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman a fort is to take away its men, removing its garrison.

clue.text: Highwaymen put stripes on it in both directions

parts.note: a band is a stripe
taken as written

indicators.note: it read one way and then the other way, backwards as well as forwards

parts.note: taken as written, then read backwards

explanation.surface: Robbers paint stripes going both ways across something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in both directions' gives IT forwards and then backwards: IT + TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is the Italian-style plural of bandit, so robbers on the road.

clue.text: This sort of investment bordered on wickedness, we hear

indicators.note: 'we hear' says the phrase before it is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: edged with guilt, i.e. guilt-edged

explanation.surface: An investment scheme that strayed close to the immoral.
explanation.walkthrough: Guilt-edged (edged with wickedness) sounds the same as the stock-market term. Gilt-edged securities are safe British government stocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilt-edged stocks are a class of very safe government security, a kind of investment.

clue.text: Merry as a monarch in a pop concert

indicators.note: 'in' puts the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a gig is a pop concert
R stands for rex or regina, a monarch

explanation.surface: As happy as a king at a rock show.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the idiom 'merry as a grig', a grig being a lively cricket or small eel.
explanation.definitionFit: The old saying 'merry as a grig' compares a cheerful person with a lively little creature.

clue.text: Frivolous place of entertainment run by the Brethren?

parts.note: light means frivolous, not serious
a house is a theatre or venue

explanation.surface: A frivolous nightspot run by a religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brethren sounds like a sect but is Trinity House, whose Elder Brethren run the coastal beacons of England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity House's Elder Brethren manage the beacons that warn ships off the coast.

clue.text: Envelop in new wildcat strike

indicators.note: a wildcat strike is unofficial and disorderly, so the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: to rap is to strike

explanation.surface: Wrap up the latest unofficial walk-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildcat' rearranges NEW into ENW, then add RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To enwrap is to wrap up, to cover or envelop.

clue.text: Container for spread

parts.note: it looks like a butter dish, but the spread is urban sprawl, held in check by a zone of open country

explanation.surface: A dish for butter or margarine.
explanation.walkthrough: A green belt is the protected countryside ring around British cities that limits their spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A green belt is a planning zone of open land that stops towns sprawling outward.

clue.text: Became infatuated by the same boy

parts.note: do is short for ditto, the same
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Fell in love with the same young man.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote is to be excessively fond, so doted means fell for someone.

clue.text: Dong's other half pursues the Camptown fellow begging

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow, so this piece comes after the one named next

parts.note: in the minstrel song Camptown Races the dialect for 'the' is 'de', so 'the man' becomes de man
ding-dong pairs the two words, so the partner of dong is ding

explanation.surface: Someone chases a man from the song Camptown Races, asking for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursues' puts DING after DEMAN. Camptown Races is an old American minstrel song ('De Camptown ladies sing dis song'), hence 'de' for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Demanding and begging both describe insistently asking for something, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Force the wife to have a break

parts.note: a rest is a break from work

explanation.surface: A husband orders his wife to take some time off.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest something is to take it by force, so wrest and force are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Game and set in new upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A match and a set played in some newly overturned setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' tells you to rearrange SETIN plus N (new).
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, an example of a game.

clue.text: Coach in Latin but becoming overworked

indicators.note: 'in' says the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: sed is the Latin word for but
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A tutor of Latin who is becoming exhausted by the workload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts TRAIN inside SED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strained has been stretched or taxed too hard, which is to be overworked.

clue.text: Lacking the staff of life, have some cake

parts.note: short of something means lacking it
bread is traditionally called the staff of life

explanation.surface: With no bread in the house, eat a slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a rich buttery biscuit, sometimes called a cake.

clue.text: Does, this person make the pulses race?

definitions.text: Does, this person make the pulses race?

parts.words: Does, this person make the pulses race?
parts.note: a person who sets pulses racing is someone attractive whom others swoon over, with a play on the pulse as a heartbeat

explanation.surface: Someone so attractive they set hearts racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartthrob is a person, usually a celebrity, whom others find thrillingly attractive.

clue.text: Is stucco a disaster for sound properties?

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruins, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Is plastering a wall bad for how a room sounds?
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges IS STUCCO A.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustics are the qualities of a room that decide how sound carries in it.

clue.text: Writes the ballad of Sir Patrick when beheaded

indicators.note: beheading a word cuts off its first letter

parts.note: Sir Patrick Spens is a traditional Scottish ballad

explanation.surface: Someone composes the old ballad about Sir Patrick at the moment of his execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when beheaded' drops the first letter of SPENS. Sir Patrick Spens is a famous Scottish border ballad about a drowned sea captain.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen something is to write it, so pens means writes.

clue.text: The airline for some going to the seaside

definitions.text: The airline for some going to the seaside

parts.words: The airline for some going to the seaside
parts.note: not a carrier flying tourists to the coast, but a tube that brings air to a swimmer face down in the sea

explanation.surface: The carrier that flies holidaymakers to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airline' tempts you to think of flights; read it as air line, a breathing tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A schnorkel is a tube that lets a swimmer breathe with the face under water.

clue.text: Like a ghost note in original psalter

indicators.note: 'in' puts the first piece inside the second
original means new and inventive, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A ghostly note found in an ancient book of psalms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' rearranges PSALTER into SPETRAL, and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectral describes a spectre, a phantom or apparition.

clue.text: Plan shows parking place

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a lot is a ... or patch of ground, a place

explanation.surface: A diagram showing where to park.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a scheme or secret plan.

clue.text: Ill-tempered chap opposed to beauty spot

parts.note: to be cross is to be at cross purposes, set against
a patch is a small black spot once worn on the face as a beauty mark

explanation.surface: A grumpy man who objects to a scenic place.
explanation.walkthrough: A beauty spot here is the fashionable fake mole (a patch), not a scenic view.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is a grumpy, bad-tempered person.

clue.text: Letter from Greece about Times leader — "A disgrace"

indicators.note: about means around, so the Greek letter goes round the other piece

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: a leader is the first, so the opening letter of the word Times

explanation.surface: A Greek correspondent writes on the newspaper's editorial and calls it shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SIGMA around T, the leader of Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame, a disgrace.

clue.text: It' may be a hotbed of reaction for the scientist

definitions.text: It' may be a hotbed of reaction for the scientist

parts.words: It' may be a hotbed of reaction for the scientist
parts.note: a hotbed of reaction suggests reactionary politics, but here it is a heated glass vessel in which a chemical reaction takes place in a lab

explanation.surface: Some place full of reactionaries, as a scientist would see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reaction' tempts you towards politics; it is chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is a small glass vessel used to hold and heat chemicals in experiments.

clue.text: Just a little finger

definitions.meaning: a small amount, a dash or trace
as a verb, to feel or handle with the fingers

explanation.definitionFit: Touch means a slight trace, as a touch of salt, and also to handle something with your hand.

clue.text: Roman general's sign, or one taking its place

indicators.note: one thing taking another's place is a substitution, so the letters named swap out

parts.note: Scorpio is a sign of the zodiac
the word or is taken as its own letters
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Roman general's emblem, or a deputy standing in for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking its place' puts I (one) where the letters OR stand in SCORPIO. The 'or' looks like a plain link word but supplies the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scipio Africanus was the Roman general who defeated Hannibal.

clue.text: Born under Victoria, true

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming after it

parts.note: the Victoria is a variety of plum

explanation.surface: Someone born in the reign of Queen Victoria, true enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts B below PLUM. Victoria is not the queen but a popular British plum variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb means exactly vertical, as true does in building.

clue.text: The boy's in a whirl

definitions.meaning: a male name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A young lad is in a spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddy is a boy's name and also a small whirlpool, a swirl of water.

clue.text: Taking advantage of an upper-class peach

parts.note: to peach is old slang for informing on someone, as is to sing

explanation.surface: Exploiting a posh young beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peach' looks like a fruit or a pretty girl, but it is a verb meaning to inform, as is 'sing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Using someone is exploiting them for your own ends.

clue.text: I had a talking bird — a downmarket one!

indicators.note: 'talking' says the words are to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: contracted, I had a becomes I'd a
a duck is a bird

explanation.surface: Someone owned a talking parrot, and a cheap one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' turns I'D A into EIDER, then add DUCK. The definition puns on eiderdown: this bird is the source of down, so a 'down-market' one.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea bird's soft breast feathers are sold as quilt filling, so it supplies the down market.

clue.text: Save the track by careful management

parts.note: to husband resources is to save them
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Rescue the railway line through sound management.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry means thrifty, careful management of resources, as well as farming.

clue.text: Bella's free 'ticket

indicators.note: free means let loose, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name Bella; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A girl called Bella has a free ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a tag or ticket attached to something to identify it.
